text:
**Short answer:** You need a power station with at least 1,800 W of continuous AC output. Battery size matters less, because induction is a heavy load but doesn't use much energy overall. An electric kettle is easier. Most kettles draw about 1,500 W or less, so any station that handles an induction plate will handle one.

**My pick from these results: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ($899).**
- Its 2,600 W inverter carries an 1,800 W induction plate with headroom, and its 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 battery is enough for several meals ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)).
- Boiling a litre of water takes only about 90–110 Wh, so you get many boils per charge (same source).
- Dealectric lists it in stock as of 2026-11-04, and the link applies a code that saves $44.95: [buy the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).
- Dealectric is the seller, so treat the "cooks for days" claim with some caution. The wattage math is still sound.

**Runtime:**
- At full 1,800 W, a 2,000 Wh-class station lasts roughly an hour of continuous cooking ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/devices/induction-cooktop)).
- Real cooking uses less. A 20-minute meal at mixed power levels uses about 300–500 Wh (same source).
- One site puts the average draw at about 1,080 W on high because the burner cycles, which gives about 1.5 hours on a 2,000 Wh unit ([BlackoutWise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop)).

**What to avoid:**
- **Small stations:** 300–600 W units like the EcoFlow RIVER 3 or Jackery Explorer 300 v2 can't run it ([Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/), [BlackoutWise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop)).
- **1,500 W units:** The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 stops at 1,500 W, so it can only run the cooktop on a lower setting ([BlackoutWise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop)).
- **The smallest that works:** Home Power Facts says the DJI Power 1000 is the smallest that can run a single burner, but only for about 0.4 hours ([Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/)).

**Tips to stretch the battery:**
- Use high power to bring food up to temperature, then drop to 400–800 W to hold a simmer. Cooking at level 5–6 instead of max can roughly halve the battery used ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/devices/induction-cooktop)).
- Keep the station's vents clear. Running near its limit makes it hot, and it may cut output to protect itself ([VanLifeKitchens](https://vanlifekitchens.com/guides/can-a-power-station-run-an-induction-cooktop)).

If you already own a 1,000 Wh station with a 1,800 W inverter, it will work for short cooking sessions. For regular cooking, I'd buy a 2,000 Wh-class unit with a 2,000 W or larger inverter.
